newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan MOF hopes for stable forex markets--Ogawa.
newsitem.headline: Japan MOF hopes for stable forex markets--Ogawa.

text.p: Japanese Vice Finance Minister Tadashi Ogawa told a news conference on Monday that he hopes for stable trading in the foreign exchange markets.
Ogawa acknowledged that the yen has strengthened against the dollar since Friday's New York trading levels.
Asked whether the moves in the foreign exchange market were excessive, Ogawa said, "It is obvious whether the move was big or small."
He said that the yen's strength was due to various views held among market participants.
"I hope that trading will be as stable as possible," Ogawa said.

He said the Group of Seven (G7) nations' meeting in Denver later this month will discuss macroeconomic issues, the stabilisation of international financial markets, debt problems and issues related to development.
Asked whether Japan's trade surplus will become a topic at the summit meeting, Ogawa said he was not aware that it would become a specific topic.
Rather, the G7 leaders will discuss various matters from the perspective of macroeconomic management, he said.
